steps.text: 'Elias, hope you're doing well.'
'I hear you went south. Right now, we might just be on opposite ends of this continent.'
'Sami is a tranquil and peaceful place. I like the environment and atmosphere here a lot. It reminds me of my home, at times.'
'I'm looking forward to Ash's reaction after she finds out we treated her map listing dangerous regions as a tourism guide.'
'Our goal is unanimous. There has to be a reason behind the crossing we made, and I'll find the answer.'
'The answers to strange questions are always hiding in strange places. Maybe one of us will be able to locate it.'
'Good luck.'
The hunter holds her breath and waits, finger on her trigger.
In her sight is a fowlbeast, wandering back and forth in the forest, leaving one footprint after another in the snow.
It too is a scavenger, seeking other life to allow its own to persist in this harsh environment.
It seems to have seen something, standing its slender neck straight, sharp beak aimed towards its prey.
In one and the same instant, it spreads its wings, and the hunter pulls the trigger.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: So close!

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Very close.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: This is some rotten luck.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Some fowl are good at catching onto how the air moves. Some have especially sensitive claws, so they can sense the slightest tremor in the ground.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: For every different kind of prey, there's a different trick to concealing yourself.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Alright, that's a lesson learned. Luck's not so bad looking at it that way—what kind of fowl did I lose just now?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: You didn't. Its time just isn't up yet.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Is that written in the prophecy too?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: You still don't believe it.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I'm just... unable to comprehend it.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: You've always seemed like a smart hunter, since we first got to know each other. Ample experience, and keen too.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Let alone how healthy you still are. I honestly can't believe it when you say it...

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Experience isn't the end-all, nor is judgment critical. Your being on this journey at this very moment is already enough.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: 'On this earth, there are special rules to survival?'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Right now, we should continue setting out north.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: If what we already know is accurate, it's just deserted tundra north of the forest. The further north we go, the less prey we can catch.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Chances are we probably just missed our last meal.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Don't be so uneasy. The prophecy only mentioned my death, but you—you'll find what you've been searching for all this time.
Several days before

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A journey to where your life ends?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: I've seen it. I've seen my death in the prophecy already. But before it happens, I have a request.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Please, take me north. We'll start from here, and bear north straight, until we emerge from the woods. If I still haven't breathed my last by then, then let us keep on northward.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: I've spent enough long, untroubled years in this little wood cabin. Before I die, I want to see some sights I've never seen before.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: I'm old and frail now. This is a journey I can't complete alone. So, I must ask for your help.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Sir, if this is truly your last wish, then of course. I'll help you any way I can.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: But what I can't understand is, how are you certain your life's almost over? I'm not even sure how much 'head straight north' can count as a dream...

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: How funny. Even in Sami, nobody would call a Sarkaz 'Sir.'

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I respect you a lot.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: The prophecy remains clear. In the end, I will surely reach the place.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: This is my final request. Take me with you, just as the prophecy showed.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: I won't have you help for nothing. At this journey's conclusion, I will provide a reward. And you will find what you've been searching for all this time.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: The place where only one moon shines.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: We're definitely advancing north, according to the compass. But the plant distribution and atmosphere in our surroundings show no stronger characteristics of a polar climate.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Whether it's the compass or common sense, something's gotta be wrong.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Sami allowed a Sarkaz to retire here—because many a thing here poses more trouble than an old devil man.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Let us go on. We haven't strayed from the course.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Why are you so sure? According to you, you'd never been here before, nor were you at all familiar.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: True, I have never set foot beyond the forest.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: But it's not experience we depend on to recognize reality. When you realize experience cannot allow you to see reality clearly, you will be one step closer to touching upon it.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Alright. Those sound like the words of someone with experience.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Regardless, I have to admit too much of this world is beyond my common sense... So, are we still heading onward?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Yes—*cough*, *cough* *cough*... We head onward.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Maybe... we could take a break for a moment.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: A fine suggestion. We still have time, and so do I.
Frost sweeps away a patch of snow by a tree, lays a layer of fallen leaves on top of it, and invites the old hunter to sit.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: This is day nine.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Prey is dwindling for sure. Supplies are scarce too—and we still need to figure out how to get back.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Don't mind me. After we reach the end of our journey, you will return alone.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I'm sorry, I still have some doubts.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Does the prophecy have some kind of concrete information, if you believe so firmly in it?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Like this journey's destination, or what kind of preparations we should make?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Or even more fundamentally, did this prophecy tell you should go someplace, or was this journey just a wish of yours...? I'm not quite sure.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Your confusion is understandable. When most have a problem, they can only act once they receive a definite answer.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: But prophecies never give answers. Prophecies do not work that way.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: But it did state clearly you would die?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Death is hardly an answer either.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I heard the people here mention 'prophecy' before I met you, too. Is it a common skill around these parts?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Truthfully, each and every one of us is capable of prophecy. We see the dark clouds gathering, and so know rain is about to fall. It's simple as that.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I'm still finding this hard to comprehend.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Then we can stop talking about prophecy, and turn simply to our travels.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Of course. You told me before how you'd been to a lot of places, too. If you still remember, that is.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Spires that bring down the rain, lakes under the sea, trenches buried beneath the ground, cities on the backs of behemoths. And as well as that, 'a nonexistent home.'

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: The stories all start intriguing, but you never finish telling them.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Of course I remember them, whether they were travels or stories.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: A journey should conclude when it's still worth reflecting on, and a story should end when its audience is still interested.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Ooh, that's definitely not an excuse to dismiss your audience.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Then let us pass the time. Allow me to finish telling my last story.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Remind me, where did I get to? No, no need. I remember now.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: In the end, I accompanied that cursed, vile beast as it found that caster. Indignantly, it asked: 'Where, after all, is my home?'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: 'All beings have an origin. Since they have an origin, there must be a place they are born. Yet why do I not? Could it be my existence was never meant?'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: The Caster answered: 'This is the rule of the curse. You exchanged your home for wisdom, and the power to make all people fear. But now you forever lost your home; true, you should not exist!'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: The beast was full of anger, and desired to savage the Caster to death. But still it calmed down.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Revenge was of no avail. It would not solve the contradiction its own existence posed. And an irrational existence is preordained to disappear.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Finally, the cursed beast chose to run, incessantly. So long as it never stopped in any one place, no part of this land would come to mean 'home,' nor 'away' to it, anymore.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: How wise of the beast, to solve the crisis of its own existence so. However, I had no energy to continue to run with it. I could only choose to stay in my little wood hut, and while away the rest of my days.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A very metaphorical story.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Through metaphor, one is acquainted with reality.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Not through experience, but through metaphor.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: You come to understand.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: So, the end of your prophesied journey is also something to do with 'home?'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: That is exactly what I expect.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I'm still very curious. Before you settled down in Sami, just how many places did you go?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: More than enough. To the point my life could have ended at any point, and it would be no regretful thing.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: At times I was a mercenary, at times a hunter, and times more still a simple traveler.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Both you and I share that passion for adventure, it seems.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: 'A scene never before seen is a priceless treasure.'

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: We had to go far no matter what, to appreciate something worth the view.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Just as that vile beast that could never stop.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Another layer of metaphor.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Well, then. It's your turn.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Fellow traveler, surely you have plenty of stories worth sharing yourself.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I've definitely got plenty of stories about my travels I could tell, but I'm worried they might be just as hard to understand for you.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: You come from a very distant place.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Distant for sure. Farther away than we can even perceive.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Then perhaps, you could say, it is far enough to be ancient?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Now there's a tricky question to answer.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Never mind. I won't seek an answer. To appreciate a story hardly requires making every detail clear.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Please, continue telling.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Alright, if you're okay with listening.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I've told this story to practically no one, but if you're going to understand where I come from, then it'll serve as a fine case.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: It's not some adventure to be proud of. It starts with an emergency landing.
'A journey into the unknown always makes me happy, despite the risks that often come with it. You understand, I could never refuse the call.'
'People always find gain in their travels. At times, it's scenes that bring happiness. At times, it's other ways of looking at the world.'
'Like that wise old hunter said, we're unable to tolerate the existence of questions with no answers. Just as if every lock has some key made to match.'
'But that's only wishful thinking. It's not the logic of what nature makes. It's kind of like a Zen thing, isn't it?'
'I'm trying to figure it out now. It might help us answer our question.'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: We're here.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: So this is what's north of the forest?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: This is 'home.'

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: You mean these ruins?
Stumbling, the old hunter sits down, the long and arduous journey having taken the last of his energy.
He gazes at the ruined, broken walls before him, his expression like a man admiring the most beautiful scenery.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: Atop these ruins, there once was a grand city.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: More than once it was destroyed, and more than once it was rebuilt.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Would a city really go in a place as desolate as this?

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: And below the barrage of fire was once a sea of flowers, and above the scorched earth were once skyscrapers.

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: 'Kazdel.'

steps.name: Old Sarkaz Hunter
steps.text: As the prophecy told, it will in the end become the home of all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Hold on, something's wrong—
In an instant, the boundless scenery surrounding her collapses.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: What's going on...
Frost looks all around. Before her, and behind her, all that remains is endless tundra.
The path they came by is gone without a trace, like the morning dew, and the magnet of the compass in her hands is deathly still, pointed straight ahead.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: The good news is we probably didn't lose our way.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: If this is also part of the metaphors you talked about... Sir?
Frost only now realizes that the old man beside her is no longer breathing.
The old hunter looks towards the cold empty expanse, his face full of serenity.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A journey to where your life ends.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: This is your last wish granted, then.
Frost sits down to the side of the old hunter, and the two hunters together admire the landscape at the end of their journey.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: There's—only one moon in the sky.
Opposite where the sun sets, a single moon appears faint on the horizon. A pale silver silhouette, in the same shade as the boundless tundra.
Frost only learns later that upon this great land, this is a sight so very rarely seen.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: 'A scene never before seen is a priceless treasure.'

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Alright. This is a reward I'm willing to take.
